source_text: However, critics contend that proxy consent is ethically invalid for non-therapeutic interventions lacking immediate medical necessity, as it substitutes parental preferences—often cultural or religious—for the child's autonomous right to an intact body, paralleling prohibitions on other non-consensual genital alterations. [140]
